title: AMD EPYC 9006 Results Are Here and AMD Delivers a Knockout Part Deux
gist: STH's launch review opener for AMD's EPYC 9006 'Venice' (Zen 6, TSMC N2, SP7 socket): up to 256 cores, 16 channels DDR5-8000/MRDIMM-12800, PCIe Gen6, 600W, framed as AMD's biggest EPYC leap since Rome and arriving amid AI-driven server CPU demand. AMD bumped the EPYC 9686F to 5.3GHz on better-than-expected Zen 6 CCD silicon and expects to exceed 50% x86 server CPU revenue share; the captured text ends before benchmark results.

insights.claim: AMD's EPYC 9006 'Venice' moves to the Zen 6 microarchitecture on 2nm with up to 256 cores/512 threads per socket, 16 channels of DDR5-8000 or MRDIMM-12800, 8TB memory capacity, PCIe 6.0 x96, a new SP7 socket and 600W peak power, versus Turin's 192 cores, 12x DDR5-6400, PCIe 5.0 x128 and 500W.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Socket power climbing to 600W and 16 memory channels raise per-server content (DIMMs, power delivery, cooling) — positive for memory and platform suppliers.

insights.claim: Venice's core complex grows to 32 cores with 128MB L3 versus 16 cores with 32MB in Genoa and Turin, and AMD uses heavier chiplets plus advanced packaging to fully exploit TSMC's N2, its first GAAFET-based node.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Venice is a significant TSMC N2 and advanced-packaging consumer — supports TSMC leading-edge and CoWoS-type demand beyond GPUs.
insights.locator: Now in its sixth generation of Zen-architecture

insights.claim: Venice delivers up to 256 cores per socket, 33% more than EPYC 9005 Turin, plus about 20% higher IPC and higher clocks, and more than twice the memory bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Generational throughput jump strengthens AMD's case for server consolidation refreshes.

insights.claim: AMD is splitting the EPYC 9006 lineup into multiple families across two primary sockets (SP7 now, the more restrained SP8 early next year), reviving high-cache -X parts with Venice-X, and adding the LPDDR5X-based Verano.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A broader SKU family lets AMD attack more sub-segments (HPC, cache-heavy, AI host) — more TAM coverage vs Intel.
insights.locator: We have lots of numbers for this one

insights.claim: STH calls Venice the most ambitious EPYC innovation since the move to an I/O die that let EPYC 7002 deliver a 'knockout', framing it as 'Knockout Part Deux'.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Reviewer sentiment points to a strong competitive position for AMD's server CPU franchise.
insights.quote: The new series covers a lot more and is by far the most ambitious innovation in the EPYC line since the switch to an I/O die
insights.locator: We have lots of numbers for this one

insights.claim: STH describes an unprecedented explosion in demand for server CPUs for AI systems, both as host nodes and to run agentic workloads, putting AMD in a commanding position with Venice arriving when the industry needs it most.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Agentic AI is reviving server CPU demand — a tailwind for x86 CPU vendors beyond the GPU trade.
insights.locator: Following AMD’s biennial CPU development roadmap

insights.claim: The server boom has inverted AMD's CPU development cycle so that the newest Zen architecture debuts first in a server CPU rather than in client parts, with Zen 6 to drive products from Venice and Verano to desktops and laptops over the next two years.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Server is now AMD's lead product priority — reflects where profits are concentrated.
insights.quote: the server boom has turned the CPU development cycle on its head
insights.locator: As far as server CPU launches go

insights.claim: AMD's Advancing AI event has become its marquee event of the year, which STH reads as a reflection of how important server parts have become to AMD's bottom line.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Data center is the earnings driver for AMD; server launches matter more than client for the stock.
insights.locator: AMD EPYC 9006 “Venice”: The Story So Far

insights.claim: Beyond AI, AMD added PCIe Gen6, new virtualization and security features, and in recent months acquired a software engineering firm to develop software to replace DRAM with flash memory.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AMD tiering DRAM to flash could, if successful, temper DRAM content per server and lift NAND usage — a second-order memory-market signal to watch.
insights.quote: it has even picked up a software engineering firm in recent months to develop software to replace DRAM with flash memory
insights.locator: AMD is keen to tap into the agentic era

insights.claim: AMD already holds 46% of x86 server CPU revenue share and expects Venice to push it above 50% for the first time within the next 12 months, while its data center division projects revenues surpassing Intel's in Q4 of this year.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A crossover above 50% revenue share would be a symbolic milestone; watch Q4 data center revenue vs Intel as confirmation.
insights.quote: AMD is already at 46% of the revenue share for the x86 server CPU market
insights.locator: AMD Venice Launch Deck – AMD Server CPU Revenue Share

insights.claim: AMD raised the flagship high-frequency EPYC 9686F (96 cores) from an announced 5.0GHz to 5.3GHz because final Zen 6 CCD silicon came in better than expected, making the fastest Venice clock higher than the fastest Turin.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Better-than-expected N2 silicon yields/bins are a positive read-through for TSMC N2 maturity and AMD margins on high-frequency SKUs.
insights.quote: As it turns out, AMD was sandbagging things a bit.

insights.claim: The shipping SP7 stack tops out with the EPYC 9996 at 256 cores, 4.1GHz boost, 1024MB L3 and 600W, alongside a 192-core EPYC 9966 (768MB L3, 600W) and a 96-core 4.8GHz EPYC 9G76.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: 1GB of L3 on a single socket targets cache-sensitive and consolidation workloads.

insights.claim: Only the EPYC 9686F received the clock bump; the 64-core EPYC 9586F stays at 5.0GHz, so customers wanting AMD's highest-clocked Venice must buy the 96-core part.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Pushes high-frequency buyers to a larger, pricier SKU — mix/ASP positive for AMD.
insights.locator: Only the EPYC 9686F is getting a specification bump
